status: retrospective redesign of figures from recorded results
timing: Written after the checkpoint results were known. The expected and surprising patterns below are interpretive contrasts, not preregistered predictions.
question: How does ask-versus-got error change with more training epochs, and what mismatch remains?
evidence: metrics.json; the same sampling seed at every checkpoint, from one training run

frames.name: When training helps
frames.takeaway: Error drops early, with no clear further improvement among the later checkpoints.
frames.expected_pattern: If each additional training period improves agreement, the observed error continues downward.
frames.surprising_pattern: The later observations flatten, rise, or resume improving instead of continuing the early reduction.
frames.observed_design: Retain true epoch spacing and uncertainty. Directly annotate the early reduction and the uncertain late comparison. Keep the target visible.
frames.limits: The lowest observed one-seed error does not establish an optimal epoch or equivalence between later checkpoints.

frames.name: The mismatch that remains
frames.takeaway: Later checkpoints still undershoot higher requests within the scored range.
frames.expected_pattern: If more training closes the mismatch, the later curve approaches achieved equals requested.
frames.surprising_pattern: The late curves remain close together below the higher requests, while their errors barely change.
frames.observed_design: Show epochs 34 and 80 together by default. Directly label their achieved win rates at the same request. Visually separate the sparse upper requests.
frames.limits: This is an observed failure pattern, not an identified causal explanation of why the model undershoots.

sketch: more training -> early reduction -> further gain uncertain
teaser.takeaway: Early improvement does not close the ask-versus-got gap.
teaser.expected_pattern: A reader can connect the early-to-late trajectory to the remaining request-versus-achievement miss.
teaser.surprising_pattern: A reader interprets the lowest observed point as a proven best training length or assumes the late mismatch is resolved.
teaser.observed_design: Compose the annotated trajectory and one shared-request example into a single figure that can stand alone in an issue comment.

hierarchy: the full data and reproduction details
visual_rules.palette_checks: Validate contrast in rendered light and dark versions; retain text labels and line styles so color is not the only identifier. A dataviz helper was not available in this session.
visual_rules.type: Use the typography hierarchy, size scale, spacing and line-length checks; preserve text as text in SVG exports.
visual_rules.export: checkpoint-error.svg and checkpoint-teaser.svg retain vector lines and text; PNG companions are used for issue embeds.

narrative_check.figures_alone: The early reduction, uncertain later comparison and unresolved miss must be legible without the issue prose.
narrative_check.words_alone: The issue prose must explain those same observations, including one-run uncertainty and the separate pooled sampling repeats.
narrative_check.data_change: None. This redesign changes presentation and annotation only.
